title: Another Look at App Integration in Business Central – Part 2
summary: This post demonstrates how to integrate two independent Business Central apps without creating a direct dependency between them by using interfaces and a shared app integration layer. The approach allows apps to register and discover each other's functionality at runtime using enums, dictionaries, and version management.
key_points: Apps can integrate without direct dependencies by implementing interfaces defined in a shared app integration layer
An App Integration codeunit uses a dictionary to store and manage implementations of interfaces from different apps
Version numbers in interface names enable future contract changes while preventing breaking changes
Consuming apps check for interface implementation before calling external app functionality, with fallback logic if unavailable
The pattern separates concerns with each app owning specific responsibilities through single responsibility principle

quotes.text: The challenge that we are trying to solve is to allow Business Central apps to call each other's functionality without creating a dependency.
quotes.why_it_matters: This defines the core problem the solution addresses - enabling optional app integration without tight coupling

quotes.text: Each app should have a clear set of responsibilities which does not overlap with the responsibilities of another app.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the architectural principle driving the design - separation of concerns ensures maintainability and independent deployment
